key_insight: AlphaDefect reports expert-level Slay the Spire 2 performance using one PPO-trained network per character to make every decision throughout a run.
engineering_relevance: The results highlight the importance of structured entity representations and engine-computed consequences for reinforcement learning in complex, stochastic environments.
method: Train one proximal policy optimization (PPO) network per character for combat and noncombat decisions.
Encode cards, relics and enemies using learned identity embeddings, game attributes and engine-computed public-information consequences.
Evaluate greedy play and test-time search on seeds excluded from training.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 62–77% greedy and 68–80% search-assisted win rates across six characters at Ascension 10 on two game versions, after 1.3–6.7 billion training decisions per character, versus 11–20% for uploaded human runs.
watch_item: The uploaded human runs are not an expert-matched baseline, and reliance on game-engine features may complicate transfer to other environments.
paper_title: AlphaDefect: Expert-Level AI for Slay the Spire 2
